questions.question: What does a graded relevance label represent?
options: The position the ranker gave the result before any rank discount is applied
A level of usefulness the result has for the query, not merely relevant or not
The share of query terms the document contains, scaled onto a zero-to-three range
The confidence the retrieval model attached to its own score for that result

questions.question: Why does DCG discount results at later ranks?
options: Because documents placed later in a list carry systematically lower grades
Because the discount rescales every graded label onto a binary relevant axis
Because the ideal ordering used for normalization contains no results past rank one
Because user attention and realized utility generally decline as the rank grows

questions.question: Using exponential gain, what gain is assigned to relevance grade 2?
What is IDCG@k?
options: The largest DCG@k that any ordering of that query's own judged documents could reach
The DCG@k obtained after reversing the returned list into ascending order of grade
The mean DCG@k over every query in the collection, used as a shared normalizer
The DCG@k recomputed after collapsing all positive grades into one binary label

questions.question: Observed DCG@3 is 7.2 and IDCG@3 is 9.0. What is nDCG@3?
Why can treating every unjudged result as irrelevant bias nDCG against a new ranker?
options: Ideal gain is computed over the unjudged documents, which inflates the normalizer
The rank discount is switched off at positions holding unjudged results, flattening it
Unjudged results are dropped from the list, so every later relevant hit moves upward
Novel relevant documents it surfaces may sit outside the pool and be scored as zero

questions.topic: MAP vs nDCG: Choosing by Relevance Model
questions.question: Which relevance model does MAP naturally assume?
options: Graded judgments, where each level contributes gain in proportion to its label
Binary judgments, where a document either belongs to the relevant set or does not
Continuous judgments, where relevance is a probability estimated from click data
Ordinal judgments, where only the order of the grades matters and not the spacing

questions.topic: MAP vs nDCG: Choosing by Relevance Model
questions.question: When is nDCG usually preferable to MAP?
options: When every relevant document is interchangeable, so one positive label suffices
When retrieving the complete relevant set matters more than where the items land
When relevance has meaningful degrees and rank-sensitive gain reflects real utility
When no relevance judgments exist, since nDCG derives its grades from the ranking

questions.topic: MAP vs nDCG: Choosing by Relevance Model
questions.question: Two known relevant results appear at ranks 1 and 3. What is AP?

questions.topic: MAP vs nDCG: Choosing by Relevance Model
questions.question: Why might exponential-gain nDCG be unstable with poorly distinguished grades 2 and 3?
options: Exponential gain collapses the two grades onto one value, so disagreement vanishes
The gain jumps from 3 to 7 between those grades, magnifying every disagreement
Exponential gain applies only below the cutoff, leaving the top positions stable
Exponential gain leaves IDCG fixed, so disagreement moves only the numerator

questions.topic: MAP vs nDCG: Choosing by Relevance Model
questions.question: A change improves nDCG but lowers MAP after grades are binarized. What is a plausible interpretation?
options: The ranker demotes its highest-grade items while retrieving more marginal ones
One implementation must be buggy, since binarizing cannot change which system wins
The ranker promotes the highest-grade items but loses relevant-set coverage
The binarization threshold was applied inside nDCG too, so both measure one thing

questions.topic: MAP vs nDCG: Choosing by Relevance Model
questions.question: Which experimental practice best prevents metric selection from favoring a preferred system?
options: Report whichever of MAP and nDCG shows the clearer gain once both are computed
Re-judge the queries on which the preferred system loses, then rescore both
Drop the queries with the widest paired delta so the comparison stays stable
Fix the relevance labels, the metric, and the cutoff before either system is scored
